instructions:
A VS Code extension for `just`, the command runner. TypeScript 7, bundled with esbuild, linted and formatted by Biome. Zero runtime dependencies by design.

The architecture is two tiers with a hard boundary between them, and most of what can go wrong here is a violation of that boundary rather than an ordinary bug. Tier 1 (`src/parser`, `src/model`) is a pure in-process library that runs on every keystroke: no VS Code API, no I/O, no subprocesses. Tier 2 runs the `just` CLI, on demand, in trusted workspaces only.

Biome already enforces style and formatting deterministically, so style comments add nothing. Review for correctness, for boundary violations, and for the invariants in the rules below.

rules.rule: Tier 1 must never emit a semantic diagnostic. The parser may report that it could not parse something at all (an unrecoverable syntax error), but it must never report anything requiring semantic understanding: unknown recipe, undefined variable, unknown attribute, wrong argument count, invalid setting. `just` is the sole authority on whether a Justfile is valid. Flag any Diagnostic constructed outside the Tier 2 / CLI path, and any parser error message that asserts something semantic. The reason is asymmetric cost: a missing squiggle is invisible, but a wrong squiggle on correct code destroys trust in every other diagnostic.

Nothing may spawn the `just` binary in an untrusted workspace. `just` evaluates backticks and `shell()` at PARSE time, so merely reading a Justfile with the CLI executes whatever it contains. Every spawn must route through the single trust-checked helper — flag any direct use of child_process, spawn, exec, execFile, ProcessExecution or ShellExecution in a feature module, even when the workspace happens to be trusted, because the next caller will copy it. Also flag any code path that honours a workspace-scoped `just.executablePath` without a trust check (that setting is itself an execution vector), and any code that captures trust at activation rather than reading it at call time.

The parser must be total: it never throws and never returns null or undefined for any input, including malformed, truncated, or empty. Flag `throw` on the parse path, returns of null/undefined from a parse method, and any loop that is not guaranteed to advance the cursor — an unbounded loop is worse than a wrong parse, because it hangs the extension host. New AST nodes must carry a source range.

Code under src/parser and src/model must not import the `vscode` API, `child_process`, or `fs`. Tier 1 is a pure library, testable in plain Node and reusable outside the editor. Only the provider layer touches the VS Code API.

Activation must stay under 50ms and do no I/O. Nothing measures this — there is no activation-time check in CI — so review is the only thing enforcing it. Flag any file read, subprocess, network call, large table construction, or top-level await reachable from `activate()`. Flag any addition to `dependencies` in package.json; the extension must have zero runtime dependencies, and the bundle must stay under 300KB (those two are CI-enforced).

User-facing strings must go through `vscode.l10n.t()`. Flag literal strings passed to showInformationMessage, showWarningMessage, showErrorMessage, tooltips, and command titles. Retrofitting localisation is far more expensive than doing it up front.

A change to what the parser or semantic model produces needs a fixture in test/differential/fixtures, not only a unit test. The fixture is what proves we agree with the real `just` CLI and keeps proving it after the next `just` release; a unit test only encodes the author's belief about how `just` behaves. If this PR changes parser output without adding or updating a fixture, say so.

When our parser and the `just` CLI disagree, `just` is right. Flag any change that makes a differential test pass by loosening or removing a comparison, skipping a fixture, or normalising away a real difference, rather than by fixing the parser. Loosening the comparison is only acceptable when the field genuinely is not something `just` promises, and that must be stated explicitly.

TypeScript is configured with `erasableSyntaxOnly`, which forbids any syntax that emits runtime code: no `enum`, no `namespace`, no constructor parameter properties. Use a frozen object with a derived union type instead of an enum. Also note `verbatimModuleSyntax` (type-only imports need `import type`), `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` (indexing yields `T | undefined`) and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` (an optional property will not accept an explicit `undefined`).

Do not assume `just` CLI behaviour from documentation or memory — its docs lag its releases. Flag any new use of a `just` flag, output shape, or language construct that is not backed by a version check or a differential fixture. The supported floor is `just` 1.27.0; a feature newer than that needs version gating, and completion must not offer it on older binaries.
